title: Proteomic Biomarkers for Bisphenol A-Early Exposure and Women's Thyroid Cancer.
ehr_evidence: Matched pairs of thyroid tumor and adjacent non-tumor tissues were collected from women thyroid cancer patients (n=28; age, 47.4±11.6 years; papillary carcinoma, 100%; metastasis, 10.4% of the subjects), who received a surgical treatment at Hanyang University Hospital, Seoul, Korea; the study also used female ICR mice exposed to BPA in utero and in early life. No electronic/computerized individual-level health records were analyzed.
summary: A combined in vivo mouse exposome and human tissue study examining early-life bisphenol A exposure effects on thyroid proteomics and its association with women's papillary thyroid cancer.
key_findings: BPA exposure altered 17 proteins in a dose-dependent manner in female offspring mice thyroid tissues (11 upregulated, 6 downregulated), of which nine were identified including Anxa6, Atp5b, Hspa5, and Vcp.
There were no significant differences in ANXA6, ATP5B, HSPA5, or VCP gene expression between thyroid tumor and adjacent non-tumor tissues in women thyroid cancer patients (p > 0.05).
Blood BPA was detected in 90% of patients with a range of 0-10.32 ng/mL (median 1.38 µg/L).

Strong positive associations were found between blood BPA levels and gene expression of VCP (r²=0.47, p=0.02) and ANXA6 (r²=0.37, p=0.03) in thyroid tumor tissues, but not in normal tissues (VCP r²=0.24, p=0.11; ANXA6 r²=0.18, p=0.17).
captured_features: 2D-PAGE protein spots identified by Q-TOF mass spectrometry
mRNA expression of ANXA6, ATP5B, HSPA5, and VCP by qPCR
Blood bisphenol A concentrations by HPLC/FLD
Tumor vs adjacent non-tumor tissue expression
Mouse BPA doses (15, 75, 300 mg/L drinking water)
study_design: Combined in vivo animal exposure study and case-control human tissue study
population: Female ICR mice exposed in utero and during early life, and women thyroid cancer patients (n=28; mean age 47.4±11.6 years; 100% papillary carcinoma) at Hanyang University Hospital, Seoul, Korea
exposure_domain: Chemical - bisphenol A (endocrine disrupting chemical), early-life/prenatal exposure
limitations: Very small human tissue sample size (n=28), acknowledged as a limitation requiring confirmation in larger cohorts.
Human gene expression differences between tumor and non-tumor tissues were null, limiting biomarker validation.
